I got SEVERE FOOD POISONING after eating here last Wednesday. This restaurant has been warned by other customers multiple times about serving food at improper temperatures going back 5 months, as several 1-star comments here show. The ramen I got should have been served piping hot as per Japanese tradition. It was just warm enough for me to not bother sending it back. HUGE mistake. I'm now on day four of being sick with diarrhea, nausea, fatigue, and stomach cramps. It is NOT WORTH THE RISK to eat at a restaurant like this that demonstrates such NEGLIGENCE when it comes to protecting the public! Some 180 people every year DIE from food poisoning in the UK alone and this establishment is obviously NOT taking its warnings seriously! I have filed a complaint with the Aberdeen City Council as should anyone else who has been served food at an improper temperature regardless of whether they got sick or not.

Regarding the restaurant's response: I am pleased the health department acted swiftly, but I doubt they arrived at 5:30pm, which was when I was there. Also, as my review was left before their inspection, the restaurant had ample warning and time to prepare for it. The fact remains that multiple guests had already complained of food being served at improper temperatures going back 5 months prior to my visit and as of the date of my visit, that issue had still not been corrected and as a result I was horribly ill for several days. I don't consider that 'holding high standards for food safety.'

This was our first time visiting Maki & Ramen after hearing some good reviews, and overall it was a pleasant experience.

The restaurant is nicely decorated with a welcoming atmosphere, and the staff were friendly and quick to seat us. We weren't overly hungry, so we ordered two dishes: the Hell Ramen and the Rainbow Roll.

The Rainbow Roll was interesting to look at because of how the toppings were assembled. Instead of each piece having the same topping, they were mixed throughout the roll, with some pieces topped with salmon and others with tuna, as shown in the photos. This made it a little difficult to appreciate the individual flavours of each type of maki, but overall it tasted fresh and was enjoyable.

The Hell Ramen was the highlight of the meal and made the visit worthwhile. It had a great level of spice, the broth was rich and full of flavour, and the toppings were fresh, and well presented.

Overall, we left satisfied with our meal. The food was good quality, reasonably priced, and the service was welcoming. We'd happily visit again and would recommend giving it a try.

I went for the first time yesterday and had an incredible time- I'm an electric wheelchair user, and from the moment I went in the staff were incredibly attentive and accomodating.

Really disappointed with our visit to Maki & Ramen Aberdeen. We’ve been to the Glasgow restaurant before and absolutely loved it, so we were really looking forward to coming here, especially as we don’t get many days out together.

Unfortunately, the experience was disappointing from the start. The restaurant was extremely cold and the air conditioning was absolutely freezing, to the point that it was uncomfortable sitting there. There was also no beer available, which was annoying, although we ordered some wine instead.

The food was where things really went downhill. My partner’s egg arrived cold, and the prawns and other seafood had a really strange texture and tasted as though they had been pre-cooked and left sitting for some time.

When our waiter asked how the meal was, we were honest and explained the issues with the food. His response was simply, “That’s odd,” and nothing further was offered or done, which we found quite disappointing considering we had clearly said we weren’t happy with the meal.

My partner then became very unwell after eating, which unfortunately spoiled what had been a rare day out together. Of course, we can’t say for certain what caused this, but given our concerns about the seafood during the meal, it certainly added to our disappointment.

We really begrudged paying what we did for an experience and meal that were so poor. It’s particularly disappointing because we love the Glasgow restaurant and had expected the same standard in Aberdeen. Sadly, based on this visit, we wouldn’t rush back.

Lovely Food, but Disappointing Customer Service

Today, we visited Maki & Ramen with friends. This wasn’t our first visit, and there’s a reason we decided to come back! The food was absolutely lovely, as always, and the atmosphere was really nice too. Unfortunately, our experience took a disappointing turn when it came time to pay.

When we approached the till and asked about our bill, the gentleman serving us already seemed visibly unhappy and irritated. However, things got even worse when we politely asked if we could pay separately. His reaction was completely unnecessary. He threw the card machine aside and looked at us as though we had asked for our food for free!

We were honestly shocked by his attitude. Asking to split a bill is a perfectly normal request, and no customer should be made to feel uncomfortable or unwelcome for simply asking.

Thankfully, another gentleman came over, and he was the complete opposite — very friendly, polite and happy to help us with exactly what we had asked for. We really appreciated his kindness and professionalism.

Unfortunately, despite the delicious food and lovely atmosphere, the behaviour of the first staff member left a very unpleasant feeling and spoiled what had otherwise been a great visit.

We genuinely enjoy coming to Maki & Ramen, which makes this experience even more disappointing. Good food brings customers in, but good customer service is what makes them want to return.

Hopefully, this is something management will take seriously, as no customer deserves to be treated that way.

I am writing about an incident at the Aberdeen branch on 12 October 2026 at approximately 20:10, while working as a part-time delivery driver.

When I arrived, only two or three tables were occupied, yet the servers were gathered near the bar and I had to wait around 8–10 minutes just to get someone’s attention. When a server finally approached, I told him the order was ready and likely on the collection shelf. He checked the bag, insisted it was not the correct order, and walked away without properly resolving the issue.

I tried to get another server’s attention, but he also initially ignored me. When he eventually came forward, he likewise claimed the bag was incorrect and appeared reluctant to check it properly. I had to insist that he verify the order number before he finally acknowledged that it was the correct bag.

What disappointed me most was not simply the wasted time, but the lack of assistance, communication and professionalism throughout the interaction. Having several years of management experience myself, I understand that mistakes happen, but staff should be willing to check an order properly rather than dismissing a delivery driver who is simply trying to do their job.

Delivery drivers’ time matters too, and we should not have to repeatedly chase staff for basic assistance or insist on a straightforward order-number check.

I strongly encourage the management team to review this incident, including any available CCTV and order records, and address the staff conduct and collection procedures at this branch.

I hope management takes this feedback seriously and ensures that delivery drivers are treated with the courtesy and professionalism they deserve.
